sources.entry: Fotohaus - Open-source photo organizer that works on your existing folders, with on-device face recognition, search and non-destructive editing. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/aelnagish/Fotohaus) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Fotohaus is an open-source, privacy-focused photo organizer for macOS that works directly on existing folders, with on-device face recognition, smart search, and non-destructive editing.
summary.what_it_does: It indexes photos in folders already on the Mac without importing them into a hidden library, and every edit is reversible. Faces are detected and recognized on-device, and a name assigned once is suggested for the same person across other photos. Search covers people, places, tags, dates, objects and scenes, and text inside photos using Apple's on-device Vision, with an optional natural-language mode. It groups RAW+JPEG pairs, bursts and Live Photos into stacks, offers a Memories "on this day" view, and has a Touch ID-locked Private collection and a 30-day Recently Deleted holding area. Editing includes one-click fixes, fine tuning, creative effects and non-destructive undo, and the app can export collages, slideshows, movies, prints and web galleries. A command-line tool (fotohaus-cli) provides search and an MCP server for AI assistants.
use_cases: organize a large photo library on a Mac
find photos of a specific person
search photos by objects, scenes or text in them
hide private photos behind Touch ID
create slideshows or movies from photos
how_to_run: xattr -cr /Applications/Fotohaus.app (if macOS reports the app as damaged)
notable: Works on existing folders in place with no hidden library import and reversible edits
On-device face recognition, offline place names from a built-in atlas, and Vision-based text and object search
Reads Picasa .picasa.ini metadata and writes it back
Command-line tool with MCP server support for AI assistants
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14 Sonoma or newer
Not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks the first launch and needs a workaround
Version 1.0.1 release described in the README
